answer:
Headline results for run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (Brady Hot Springs PoroTomo DAS, March 2016):

Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window).
Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 detections above the catalogue completeness magnitude Mc).
Pumping over the 15.96-day window: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 (net extraction).
Catalogue (LBNL/NCEDC, GDR 859, March 2016): 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07.

CALIBRATED probabilities (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated one):
  b     Sigma     P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) in observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0   -5.449    0.0001198       5.236e-06                       0.03719
  0.73  -5.319    0.004922        0.0002155                       0.2809
  0.65  -5.281    0.01474         0.0006484                       0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated DAS magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts — this is the upper bound, not calibrated):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842.

Interpretation: the calibrated catalogue-based estimate puts P(Mw >= 5.5) at ~1.2e-4 to ~1.5e-2 per year depending on the b scenario (b = 1.0 to 0.65), while the DAS-based upper bound is 0.07842 per year. The DAS number is an upper bound because its magnitudes are uncalibrated and it treats every DAS detection as an event at or above Mc, inflating the count; the catalogue-based (LBNL) numbers are the calibrated ones.
